articleTitle: Viability of Long Short Term Memory Networks in the Health Prediction of Lithium-ion Batteries
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on E-mobility, Power Control and Smart Systems (ICEMPS)
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries play a crucial role in diverse aspects of present day life owing to their distinctive attributes and adaptable uses, spanning from everyday electronic devices to Electric vehicles(EVs) and sustainable energy systems.The life and operational features of rechargeable batteries are significantly influenced by Battery Management System (BMS). Implementation of BMS is essentially aimed at overseeing and regulating various aspects of a battery's functioning to optimize overall efficiency, ensure safety, and prolong battery life. The principal concern associated with batteries is battery degradation, which is the slow deterioration of a battery's capacity over time, making it harder for it to hold a charge. It is a natural and inevitable process that occurs due to various factors.The application of artificial intelligence for State of Health (SoH) prediction in batteries, a critical aspect in assessing their remaining useful life. The process entails thorough data collection from the battery system, including charge-discharge cycles, temperature profiles, voltage, and current data. Subsequently, relevant features are selected, and the data undergoes preprocessing to address missing values and inconsistencies.Long Short Term Memory (LSTM) networks are trained on the dataset, allowing them to learn patterns or characteristics features in voltage(v), current(I) and temperature(T) to predict battery's health.Successful implementation depends on the quality of training data and appropriate feature selection. The simulations were performed using MATLAB software and the results are presented.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Ternary Full Adder Based on FinFET Models
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on E-mobility, Power Control and Smart Systems (ICEMPS)
abstract: In the field of digital system design, the introduction of multivalue logics has shown to be beneficial as it reduces circuit complexity and improves energy efficiency. Ternary logic is usually seen as an innovative approach in the realm of multivalue logic. This article presents a comprehensive overview of the design of a ternary full adder using 18nm FinFET technology, implemented via the use of the Virtuoso tool offered by Cadence. The evaluation of the full adder's performance is carried out by a comparison of the results obtained using SVT and HVT FinFET models. The obtained simulation results reveal power consumption values of 124.9 and 113.6 μW, transient delay values of 180.1 and 180.7 ns, and power delay product values of 22.49 and 20.64 (x 10_<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sup>J) for the SVT and HVT FinFET models, respectively. The proposed design of a ternary full adder can be used for processing ternary encoded signals and designing of ternary arithmetic circuits for ternary computers.

articleTitle: Advancements in the Internet of Medical Things in Healthcare: A Comprehensive Systematic Review
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on E-mobility, Power Control and Smart Systems (ICEMPS)
abstract: The Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) has arisen as a force that is transforming the healthcare industry by providing novel solutions for patient monitoring, diagnosis, treatment, and care. This bibliometric study investigates the expanding body of scientific literature that is focused on IoMT. The results of this investigation provide insights into the research trends, significant contributors, and theme development that are occurring in the area. Examine the publishing output, geographical distribution, and patterns of cooperation among researchers and institutions by conducting an analysis of research papers, reviews, and conference proceedings that are indexed in a variety of academic databases. Additionally, study the most popular subjects and developing areas of interest within IoMT, with the goal of shining light on the vital role that technology will play in the molding of the future of healthcare. This research emphasizes not only the multidisciplinary character of IoMT but also its relevance in tackling difficulties in the healthcare industry, improving patient outcomes, and driving data-driven innovation in the healthcare sector. This bibliometric study provides academics, practitioners, and policymakers with useful insights by mapping the intellectual landscape of IoMT research. These individuals are attempting to navigate and contribute to the ever-evolving area of medical IoT.

articleTitle: Choosing LS-Stat Confidence Scores for Neural Networks Predictions
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on E-mobility, Power Control and Smart Systems (ICEMPS)
abstract: Due to the inherent opacity of Neural Network (NN) models, it can be challenging for users to have confidence in the accuracy of their predictions. The usability of AI systems powered by NN models will depend on how trustable these models are since a false positive or false negative can be significant in a critical system. This research presents improvements to the LS-Stat Confidence Score algorithm for selecting the most accurate score from an ensemble of score computation techniques. The new score selection technique discussed in this paper utilizes the distance between the latent characteristics of an input sample and that of the training data samples in each class to estimate the “nearest” class. If the estimated nearest class matches the predicted class, then the prediction is highly trustworthy and hence LS-Stat returns the highest statistical confidence score. If the estimated nearest class does not match the predicted class, the model prediction is less trustworthy and hence LS-Stat provides the lowest statistical confidence score. We apply LS-Stat algorithm to CIFAR-10, CIFAR-10C, CIFAR-100 and SVHN datasets and compare our results with the baseline Softmax prediction probabilities. We show that LS-Stat confidence scores provide better trustworthiness estimation for model predictions.

articleTitle: Ferranti Effect on a T- Section Model of an Overhead Transmission Line – A detailed Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on E-mobility, Power Control and Smart Systems (ICEMPS)
abstract: This paper presents a novel laboratory model designed for hands-on evaluation of the Ferranti Effect on transmission lines. The Ferranti Effect is characterized by a steady voltage at the open end of an uncompensated transmission line that surpasses the voltage at the sending end. The key aspect of this research lies in its empirical approach, achieved through experimentation using hardware equipped with a power generator and an advanced double bus bar system. The experimental analysis focuses on voltage regulation and the observation of voltage profiles on transmission lines. The study aims to identify the capacitive and inductive properties of the line as crucial factors in the manifestation of the Ferranti Effect, particularly under conditions of light load or open circuits at the receiving end. By doing so, it enhances the practical understanding of transmission line phenomena. This empirical investigation offers valuable insights for power engineering education, emphasizing the significance of laboratory prototypes in validating theoretical concepts.

articleTitle: Improving Bankruptcy Forecasting Through the Integration of a Resilient Analysis-Infused Classifier and Harnessing the Power of DenseNet121 Convolutional Neural Network Within Deep Learning Frameworks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on E-mobility, Power Control and Smart Systems (ICEMPS)
abstract: In the realm of evaluating financial risks, accurately predicting bankruptcy holds paramount importance for maintaining the stability of economic systems. A longstanding challenge in this field revolves around imbalanced datasets, where instances of bankruptcy are notably fewer than those of non-bankrupt cases. Mitigating this issue involves implementing a robust strategy that combines the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) with DenseNet121 CNN classification, resulting in heightened model accuracy. Financial data often exhibits an imbalance in class distribution, with occurrences of bankruptcy being significantly outnumbered by instances of solvency. This imbalance poses a substantial hurdle for machine learning algorithms, as they tend to display a bias toward the dominant class, leading to suboptimal accuracy in forecasting the minority class (bankruptcy). The primary objective of this study is to leverage DenseNet121 CNN for bankruptcy detection classification. This goal will be accomplished through the application of SMOTE Analysis, specifically designed to address the challenges posed by unbalanced data. The study aims to achieve an anticipated accuracy of 84 percent, employing the classification report and the confusion matrix as visualization tools in the proposed research. These metrics will contribute to a comprehensive understanding of the results and further enhance the reliability of the bankruptcy prediction model.

articleTitle: Evaluating the MobileNet50 CNN Model for Deep Learning-Based Maize Visualisation and Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on E-mobility, Power Control and Smart Systems (ICEMPS)
abstract: Plant diseases present a substantial threat to global food security, and the timely detection of such diseases remains a challenging and time-consuming task. The accurate determination of a plant's health status and the identification of specific infections typically require the expertise of professionals. The advent of Deep Learning has significantly transformed the field of computer vision, offering highly efficient techniques for image analysis and categorization. This study specifically focuses on utilizing the MobileNet50 Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model to visually represent and categorize images of maize. The identification of maize, a widely cultivated crop, is intricate due to its diverse array of varieties and growth stages. This research aims to leverage the capabilities of the advanced MobileNet50 CNN architecture to enhance the precision and effectiveness of maize classification. The model achieved an impressive accuracy of 97%, demonstrating its robust performance in distinguishing various types and health states of maize plants. By employing MobileNet50, this study contributes to the advancement of computer vision applications in agriculture, facilitating the prompt and accurate identification of maize diseases. The utilization of a deep learning approach reduces the dependency on human expertise, making it more accessible and efficient for large-scale agricultural monitoring. Ultimately, the integration of MobileNet50 in maize classification holds promise for revolutionizing plant disease detection and contributing to global efforts in securing food resources.

articleTitle: Advanced Monkeypox Classification using EfficientNet B3: A Promising Method
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on E-mobility, Power Control and Smart Systems (ICEMPS)
abstract: A rare and potentially fatal viral disease, monkeypox predominantly impacts non-human primates, including humans. It is critical to establish an early and precise diagnosis of monkeypox in order to contain outbreaks and administer opportune treatment effectively. Deep learning and convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have demonstrated considerable potential in the domain of medical image diagnosis in recent times. The current research paper introduces an innovative methodology for categorizing images of monkeypox utilizing the cutting-edge deep learning framework, EfficientNetB3. Outstanding performance has been exhibited by EfficientNetB3, a CNN architecture renowned for its high efficiency and accuracy across a range of image classification tasks. This study presents the adaptation and fine-tuning of EfficientNetB3 to classify monkeypox. Data augmentation techniques are implemented to improve the model's capacity to extrapolate to diverse variations present in images of monkeypox. A substantial collection of images about monkeypox, comprising laboratory samples and clinical photographs, is utilized by the proposed model. In terms of accurately and precisely classifying images of monkeypox, experimental results demonstrate the efficacy of our method. Several metrics are employed to assess the efficacy of the mode. The performance of the trained EfficientNetB3 model in differentiating monkeypox from various skin conditions and infections is encouraging, as this capability is critical for the timely and precise diagnosis of the disease.

articleTitle: Analysing the Electrical Fault Detection and Classification Capabilities of a Decision Tree Classifier
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on E-mobility, Power Control and Smart Systems (ICEMPS)
abstract: The identification of faults in traditional approaches often depends on intricate algorithms and considerable preparation of data. On the other hand, decision tree classifiers provide a more simple but effective method for automated fault identification and classification. The aim of this study is to evaluate how well a Decision Tree Classifier performs in the field of detecting and categorizing electrical faults. Electrical systems are vulnerable to a multitude of errors that have the potential to compromise the dependability and security of the whole infrastructure. The study utilises a dataset that consists of electrical signals obtained from various failure situations, such as short circuits, overloads, and ground faults. The information is used to train the Decision Tree Classifier, which aims to construct a prediction model for the purpose of recognising and categorising various forms of electrical failures. The research assesses the performance of the model by analysing important metrics like accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score. The results indicate that the Decision Tree Classifier is capable of efficiently recognizing and classifying electrical defects, showcasing its adaptability in different fault scenarios. The results of this study provide significant contributions to the understanding of how decision tree classifiers may be used in the context of problem detection in electrical systems. These findings emphasise the efficacy of decision tree classifiers as a means of improving the dependability and robustness of power distribution networks. The study findings have significant implications for enhancing maintenance techniques and advancing the development of intelligent systems that provide real-time problem monitoring in electrical infrastructure.

articleTitle: Incorporating the CatBoost Classification Method in Machine Learning Applications for Smote Analysis and Bankruptcy Data Equalisation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on E-mobility, Power Control and Smart Systems (ICEMPS)
abstract: In the context of financial risk assessment, the ability to predict bankruptcy has considerable significance in ensuring the stability of economic systems. One of the enduring challenges in this specific domain is imbalanced datasets, where the frequency of cases reflecting bankruptcy is much lower compared to instances representing non-bankrupt scenarios. The objective of this research is to investigate the use of the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) in combination with the CatBoost classification algorithm. The focus is on achieving data equalisation and enhancing bankruptcy prediction. The use of the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) algorithm in combination with the CatBoost algorithm efficiently leverages the distinct qualities and benefits provided by each methodology. The Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) is a technique designed to address the problem of class imbalance by creating synthetic samples for the minority class. This social strategy improves the model's capacity to gather and acquire patterns from the class that is not well represented. The CatBoost algorithm, which accesses categorical feature handling skills with an efficient boosting methodology, is used to analyse the enlarged dataset and develop a robust prediction model for the task of bankruptcy detection. The main aim of this study is to employ the Catboost classifier in order to classify Bankruptcy detection. The precision will be achieved by the use of SMOTE Analysis, a technique particularly designed to address the issue of unbalanced data. The research study will use the classification report and the confusion matrix as evaluation metrics to assess the anticipated accuracy level of 97 percent. The proposed research would use visual tools to analyse and show the results.

articleTitle: Automatic Control of Solar-Powered Battery System with Maximum Power Point Tracking
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on E-mobility, Power Control and Smart Systems (ICEMPS)
abstract: In today's world, the most severe issue with battery-inverter systems is their dependability. They tend to switch off or deliver little power during outages or other intrinsic system faults. This research paper entails designing an automatic system for powering loads using solar PV and maintaining essential power flow to loads through maximum power point tracking using an incremental conductance algorithm. When radiance levels on the PV are low the PV detects this change and automatically disconnects from the system allowing the battery to discharge and power any appliance or load connected to the system. The MPPT control automatically corrects any discrepancies, allowing for efficient operation. MATLAB Simulink is used to realize the design.

articleTitle: Increasing Photovoltaic Efficiency in FASnI3-based Solar Cells by Minimizing Interface Defect Density

The study examines the changes in the interface defect density (IDD) that occur between the active layer and the hole transport layer (HTL). The researchers used the Solar Cell Capacitance Simulator (SCAPS-1D) program to model the apparatus. SnO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> serves as the electron transport layer (ETL), FASnI<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> serves as the active layer, and Spiro-OMeTAD serves as the hole transport layer (HTL) in the optimal structure of the solar cell. articleTitle: Exploring Photovoltaic Efficiency in Perovskite Solar Cells with CsSnCl3: The Role of Absorber Layer Thickness
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on E-mobility, Power Control and Smart Systems (ICEMPS)
abstract: Cesium tin chloride (CsSnCl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>) exhibits promising characteristics as a competitive and economically feasible absorber material in the context of lead‑free PSC. Superior light absorption makes these CsSnCl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> efficient at turning sunlight into energy. The abundance of cesium and tin makes them cheap. Lead toxicity and long-term stability issues persist, but continuing research intends to remove them, making CsSnCl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> PSCs an attractive solar energy contender. A study has been carried out to examine the impact of variations in thickness on the effectiveness of the device. articleTitle: Grid Integrated Hybrid Renewable Energy System for Power Quality Improvement Using Open End Winding Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on E-mobility, Power Control and Smart Systems (ICEMPS)
abstract: Hybrid renewable systems are emerging as a promising method for replacing the conventional fossil fuel based energy economy. Integrating more than one renewable sources increases the capacity factor of the system, reduces unpredictability and improves stability of electricity supplied. Grid integration of these systems are challenging due to the voltage and frequency regulation issues. Power quality issues like unbalance, harmonic distortions, transients etc. need to be addressed while integrating these renewable sources to the utility. This paper proposes a power quality enhancement method with the help of an open end winding transformer fed hybrid renewable system. The hybrid system combines a solar photovoltaic system with a wind power plant. Active power filter based control scheme is chosen for the control of both voltage and current distortions. An open end winding transformer with open primary and star connected secondary coupled to the grid is considered. The open primary windings are supplied with two voltage source inverters which are fed with renewable energy sources. First grid-connected inverter is controlled as dynamic voltage restorer to compensate for voltage distortions. The second inverter is controlled to mitigate current distortions and also provides reactive power compensation with shunt power filter control. The proposed system is simulated and validated in MATLAB/Simulink and shows that the system minimizes the harmonic distortions within the standard limits.

articleTitle: Enhancing Hyperspectral Image Classification Performance Using Adaptive Spectral Band Selection and Clustering-based Mutual Information (ASBS-CMI)
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on E-mobility, Power Control and Smart Systems (ICEMPS)
abstract: Hyperspectral imaging is an emerging tool in remote sensing applications for acquiring detailed spectral data. This paper introduces the Adaptive Spectral Band Selection and Clustering-based Mutual Information (ASBS-CMI) approach, employing adaptive spectral band selection through clustering and mutual information to enhance hyperspectral imaging classification. The ASBS-CMI method includes preprocessing for data quality improvement, clustering to group similar pixels, mutual information calculation for identifying informative spectral bands, and subsequent feature extraction from selected bands for classification. Principal Component Analysis is meant for feature extraction to capture spatial-spectral information. Class labels are assigned to hyperspectral data using a Random Forest classifier. Experimental results on Pavia University Scenes and Indian Pines datasets, along with comparisons to Support Vector Machine and Feed Forward Neural Network, demonstrate improved accuracy within a limited time. The proposed methodology's efficiency is evidenced by evaluating performance through various metrics, showcasing its potential to advance hyperspectral image analysis in remote sensing applications.

articleTitle: Lane Detection Using Hough Transform and Kalman Filter
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on E-mobility, Power Control and Smart Systems (ICEMPS)
abstract: The objective of this paper is to implement an effective and robust lane detection system for autonomous vehicles. This can be achieved by generating road images using MATLAB, converting them into a bird's-eye view for a clear perspective of the lanes, and then applying the Kalman filter for accurate lane detection. After using the Hough transform and Kalman filter the lanes on a video clip that has been recorded from inside a car using a phone camera will be detected. The system is implemented in real-world scenarios to ensure its effectiveness and reliability in various road conditions and environments. The goal is to improve road safety and navigation by providing precise lane information.

articleTitle: DC-DC Converter with Wide Voltage Conversion Ratio and Improved Current Capability for Charging Ultracapacitor Bank
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on E-mobility, Power Control and Smart Systems (ICEMPS)
abstract: This paper presents the design and hardware implementation of a DC-DC converter operating in continuous conduction mode (CCM) intended to provide wide voltage conversion and improved current capability for ultracapacitor charging application. The design method of the converter is analysed for a desired output voltage and current, based on the voltage and current ripple specifications. Steady state performance of the converter is studied based on the hardware open loop configuration. A constant current mode control loop is designed to study the dynamic performance of the converter in closed-loop simulation using MATLAB/Simulink environment. Experimental and simulation waveforms are illustrated for validation of the designed converter along with efficiency calculation.

articleTitle: Mapping AI's Influence on Cardiac Healthcare: A Bibliometric Analysis (2014-2023)
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on E-mobility, Power Control and Smart Systems (ICEMPS)
abstract: Artificial intelligence in one of the fast-growing fields. In medical and smart healthcare field artificial intelligence has gained considerable momentum. The utilization of technological advances in cardiology has gained significance as a study topic recently. Smart healthcare seeks to increase the health and well-being of people throughout their lives by utilizing cutting-edge technology like AI. The use of artificial intelligence during medical procedures will enhance illness diagnosis, categorization, and prediction, which is advantageous to both patients and healthcare professionals. One of the primary objectives of bibliometric analysis is to assess and comprehend the academic significance of research publications, authors, journals, and academic institutions. The goal of the study was to carry out a bibliometric analysis on healthcare-related, heart disease, or cardiac disease research with AI predication and deep learning from the years 2014 to 2023.

articleTitle: Review of Autonomous Mobile Robots
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on E-mobility, Power Control and Smart Systems (ICEMPS)
abstract: Almost half a century has elapsed since the initial surge of curiosity in autonomous robots was observed, and the pursuit to improve these devices' ability for fully aware decision-making continues, particularly with regard to the safety of users. Given their current state of development, autonomous robots are becoming more and more common in social settings. This article summarises the technology's present development status and traces the growth of interest in it. We examine and talk about certain applications of it, like its functionality and state of development. Lastly, difficulties with the state of the art and novel approaches that are still being worked on are emphasised in order to facilitate a broader use of these autonomous robots.

articleTitle: Torque Ripple Reduction of SynRM Using Rotor Structure Modification
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on E-mobility, Power Control and Smart Systems (ICEMPS)
abstract: The automobile industry is shifting toward electric vehicles (EVs), albeit not everyone can afford them. The motor, which is one of the essential components of an EV along with the battery, is currently mostly dependent on permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSMs), which raises the cost of EVs because permanent magnets are expensive. These days, synchronous reluctance motors (SynRMs) are an excellent alternative to PMSMs because of their great efficiency and lack of permanent magnets. However, a significant issue with SynRM is the high torque ripple. Reducing torque ripple can be achieved using suitable controls and structural modification. To reduce torque ripple, this article discusses the performance of two new SynRM rotor structures and proposes the best rotor structure for electric car applications. The torque ripple of SynRM models is analyzed using Ansys Electronics Desktop and compared with the conventional SynRM.

articleTitle: Playing Cards Classification and Detection Using Sequential CNN Model Through Machine Learning Techniques Using Artificial Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on E-mobility, Power Control and Smart Systems (ICEMPS)
abstract: The task of identifying and classifying playing cards within images or video streams in computer vision involves employing a Sequential Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model. This process combines image categorization and object recognition, presenting a sophisticated and engaging implementation of machine learning techniques. The significance of classifying and detecting playing cards extends to artificial intelligence and computer vision, with numerous practical applications. Systems for classifying and detecting playing cards utilizing artificial intelligence (AI) rely on computer vision methods and deep learning algorithms to achieve precise identification and categorization. These technological solutions not only enhance automation and efficiency across various tasks but also open up new possibilities for interaction and enjoyment in the domain of playing card games, making them accessible and engaging in diverse industries and user experiences. The primary objective of this research is to categorize playing cards and predict their expected accuracy, targeting a result of 75 percent. The high level of accuracy demonstrated in this study holds potential benefits for future researchers exploring this technology and subject matter.

articleTitle: Optimization of PI Controller for Coupled Tank Systems Using Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on E-mobility, Power Control and Smart Systems (ICEMPS)
abstract: In present work, Genetic Algorithm (GA) is utilized to construct a Proportional-Integral (PI) controller for a Coupled Tank System (CTS). Its effectiveness is evaluated and compared with a conventional PI controller. The performance of the proposed GA-PI controller is also benchmarked against previous research. The CTS, a standard process control system, is employed to regulate liquid levels in tanks. The controller based on GA approach offers a viable alternative to traditional PI controller tuning techniques that may not be appropriate for this task. Here, PI controller parameters have been optimized using the GA to obtain the desired control performance. Comparative analysis is conducted between the traditional PI controller and the GA-PI controller. The steady-state response analysis reveals that the PI controller tuned via GA surpasses the performance of the traditional PI controller. Additionally, the research findings indicate that utilizing a GA for PI controller tuning results in superior control performance compared to conventional methods. Additionally, it is noted that the suggested GA-based PI controller demonstrates superior performance compared to previous studies in terms of rise time, settling time, and overshoot, particularly with respect to minimizing the Integral of Absolute Error.

Author Keywords: Integral Absolute Error (IAE) and Integral Square Error (ISE) performance

articleTitle: The Use of a K-Nearest Neighbour Classifier and Other Machine Learning Techniques for Exploratory Data Analysis of Red Wine Quality
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on E-mobility, Power Control and Smart Systems (ICEMPS)
abstract: This research investigates the use of a K-Nearest Neighbours (KNN) model and further Machine Learning methodologies for doing Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) on the quality of red wine. The dataset consists of a wide range of chemical and sensory characteristics that are linked to red wines. The study utilises rigorous data preparation techniques, such as addressing missing values and outliers, to prepare the dataset for analysis. The K-nearest neighbours (KNN) model, known for its simplicity and ability to capture local patterns, is used to reveal complex linkages within the dataset. This research assesses the efficacy of the KNN model and many other Machine Learning approaches by using appropriate measures, therefore elucidating their predictive capacities and ability to generalise to unfamiliar data. The purpose of exploratory investigations is to investigate and access the potential benefits of combining feature engineering and dimensionality reduction techniques in order to improve model interpretability and overall performance. The findings of this study provide significant contributions to our understanding of the intricate connections between chemical and sensory characteristics in red wines. These insights have practical consequences for professionals in viticulture, winemaking, and research within this domain. Additionally, this work highlights and employs the adaptability of Machine Learning in deciphering patterns within complex datasets, hence offering prospects for further investigation in the field of wine quality analysis.

articleTitle: Deep Learning for Precise Rice Multi-Class Classification:Unveiling the Potential of CNNs
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on E-mobility, Power Control and Smart Systems (ICEMPS)
abstract: This research delves into the difficult realm of classifying rice. It concentrates on five common kinds cultivated in Turkey: Arborio, Basmati, Ipsala, Jasmine, and Karacadag. The research presents a massive database of 75,000 high-resolution grain images, meticulously matched with 15,000 shots of each species of rice. The imagegraphs were carefully picked by Koklu et al. he significance of classifying these varieties lies in its paramount importance for agricultural practices and seed quality assessment. Using Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) techniques, the research illustrates how complicated and rich the dataset is. It also highlights how crucial it is to have complicated models to locate and exploit the data's complex patterns. The findings reveal an incredible 97.45% accuracy, which illustrates how effectively the CNN algorithms functioned at categorizing the various varieties of rice. Precision, recall, and F-score measurements were also assessed to provide a holistic image of how well the categorization functioned. Researchers and rice enthusiasts who wish to learn more about how to categorize rice and what it entails for cultivation and quality evaluation will find this research extremely informative.

articleTitle: Pisces Bot
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on E-mobility, Power Control and Smart Systems (ICEMPS)
abstract: The PISCES BOT stands as an integrated solution to address multifaceted challenges encountered by fish farmers, providing automation for feeding, filtration, aeration, medication, power backup during blackouts, and pond surveillance. This comprehensive system, equipped with notification capabilities, minimizes the need for constant supervision by alerting farmers when intervention is required. Featuring two feeding units, dual filtration chambers, and a dedicated medication unit, the PISCES BOT ensures precise and timely operations. The feeding mechanism, driven by servo motors, guarantees optimal nourishment for the fish. The filtration system, comprising a sponge bar and bio-ball filters, coupled with activated charcoal, enhances water quality. Agitating and oxygenating pond water by spraying filtered water from a height, the system effectively boosts dissolved oxygen content. Additionally, the medication unit facilitates targeted delivery of medicines when needed. The PISCES BOT not only addresses critical issues in fish farming but also has the potential to attract more investors to engage in this streamlined and efficient approach, fostering advancements in aquaculture practices.

articleTitle: Next-Generation Traffic Control: Adaptive Timer and Emergency Vehicle Priority in Intelligent Traffic Management
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on E-mobility, Power Control and Smart Systems (ICEMPS)
abstract: Traffic has always been a troubling issue in our society. The increased number of automobiles on roads has sub-stantially increased traffic congestion polluting the environment and causing stress and anxiety to passengers in the traffic clog. The existing system of fixed traffic control system even though widely used, lacks adaptability and operates on predefined signal timers. The lack of adaptability can lead to inefficient traffic flow, especially during high traffic congestion. To address this issue, we propose a more adaptive and intelligent system that leverages adaptive timer control and prioritizes emergency vehicles like, ambulance. The adaptive timer control system considers the count of vehicles at the previous junction as well as the count of vehicles currently arriving at the intersection to update the signal timers. Additionally, to prevent delays in emergency response times and to provide a better impact on public safety and health outcomes we have provided an added feature to prioritize emergency vehicles and release the traffic upon its arrival at the respective signal. The detection of the emergency vehicle is to be carried out using the YOLO v8(You Look Only Once) algorithm along with siren recognition using a classifier model. The proposed system offers a significant improvement over the existing traffic control infrastructures and has the potential for aiding resilient and smooth transportation.

articleTitle: A Robotic Manipulator with Conveyor System for Visual Sorting of Work Pieces
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on E-mobility, Power Control and Smart Systems (ICEMPS)
abstract: The proposed system for sorting work pieces integrates a four-degree-of-freedom robotic manipulator with computer vision and conveyor transportation capabilities for automated object handling and sorting. Utilizing a conveyor system and inverse kinematics, the robotic arm ensures efficient movements. Real-time images of work pieces are captured and processed using computer vision techniques, allowing for size and color-based sorting. The integration of machine learning with robotic control can ensure dynamic and accurate sorting. The integrated system reduces labor costs, minimizes errors, and finds applications in manufacturing, logistics, and assembly lines improving productivity and product quality.

articleTitle: Body Language Recognition System for Communication Quality Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on E-mobility, Power Control and Smart Systems (ICEMPS)
abstract: The development of computer vision technology in recent days, enhanced the human-computer interface (HCI) systems in a broad spectrum. The recent developments of human computer interfacing such as Augmented reality applications, gesture-based control devices, robotic assistants, patient health care monitoring systems considers human body pose estimation as important process involved in it. The growth of neural computing and artificial intelligence (AI) models plays an optimum role in development of HCI and pose estimation. The presented study considers various existing challenges in body language recognition systems and its role in communication quality enhancement. The comprehensive study considers existing state of art approaches and its drawbacks, challenges, technology, tool in terms of achieving better accuracy and formulated a robust human pose estimation model using machine learning technology. The suggested architecture and solutions derived from the proposed method are well explored in the article.

articleTitle: Exploring Efficiency Optimization in Lead-Free Cs2TiBr6 Perovskite PV Cells through SCAPS-1D Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on E-mobility, Power Control and Smart Systems (ICEMPS)
abstract: The methylammonium lead halide PV has garnered significant attention owing to its lightweight characteristics, cost-efficiency, and readily replicable fabrication techniques. Despite the advantages mentioned, the commercialization of these cells remains unlikely due to concerns around the toxicity linked to lead. Cesium-titanium (IV) bromide (Cs2TiBr6) emerges as a viable substitute for lead-based perovskites. However, the lack of suitable hole and electron transport layers poses a hindrance to achieving higher Power Conversion Efficiency (PCE) in CS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>TiBr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>. The primary objective of this research is to optimize the performance of Cs2TiBr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>solar cells by examining and analysing the ideal thickness parameter. In this investigation, we employed the SCAPS-1D program to do simulations, facilitating an examination of many parameters like energy bandgap, electron affinity, doping density, and thickness. The findings of our research demonstrate that by the deliberate adjustment of the absorber layer using meticulously chosen parameters, it is feasible to attain a substantial PCE of up to 23.02%. Regrettably, certain occurrences also exhibited a decline in power conversion efficiency. Nevertheless, this research study makes a noteworthy contribution towards enhancing the efficiency of PV cell.

articleTitle: A Compact Automatic Utensil to Convert Kitchen Waste into Organic Fertilizer for Plants
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on E-mobility, Power Control and Smart Systems (ICEMPS)
abstract: The key to collect the waste from the apartment or huddle and make them decompose and convert to fertilizer is a complicated process. The proposed project is used to convert food waste into fertilizer for gardening in a short period of time. The proposed idea aims to design and fabricate a compact machine to convert kitchen waste into organic fertilizer for plants. The waste used is kitchen waste such as vegetable peels, eggshells, cooked food etc. The project comprises hopper, container, blade, blender, motor, capacitive proximity sensor and PLC. This experimental setup has an opening to dump the waste into the container. The proximity sensor senses the dumping of waste and signals the blade motor to turn on immediately. The sequence of operations are programmed and simulated using a programmable logic controller. The waste undergoes the crushing process that makes the waste to smaller size that helps to decompose easily. To produce a dry fertilizer, the excess water from the waste must be removed. Hence the waste then undergoes a heating process by using a heating coil along with the blending of the soil with waste to remove the water evenly. Coconut fiber and microbial soil is added simultaneously during the blending process to mix the waste and soil to form a rich fertilizer. After 78 hours, the waste that is blended with soil will be decomposed and converted as a fertilizer that will be ready to use in gardens

articleTitle: Load Flow of Radial Distribution Network by using Artificial Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on E-mobility, Power Control and Smart Systems (ICEMPS)
abstract: Load flow analysis has an important and significant role in assessing or evaluating power system performance. There are number of traditional methods available which has higher accuracy for transmission system. In distribution networks, due to the lack of convergence, especially for large complex systems, there is need for development of alternative methods of computation. Solving equations involving Algebraic expressions are very much simpler and requires very less computer memory. There are many such literatures available that involves solving the algebraic equations alone to find the network parameters. The objective is to develop a new methodology with higher accuracy, better computation speed and simplicity. Artificial neural networks (ANNs) can be a better alternative due to their speed and ability to model nonlinear relationships. A novel technique for solving load flow problems of radial distribution networks using ANN is presented in this work. A neural network trained in back-propagation is used to map power system parameters (bus data, line data, and power demands) to phase angles and voltage magnitudes at all buses. The model is trained using data generated from conventional load flow methods. The ANN model demonstrates high accuracy, achieving negligible errors compared to conventional load flow solutions. It also exhibits significant computational advantages, giving faster solutions than traditional iterative methods. The proposed ANN-based approach provides a fast, accurate and reliable alternative for the power flow analysis of distribution networks which are mostly radial.

articleTitle: Case Study on Predictive Modeling of UAV Battery Remaining Useful Life Using Machine Learning Regression Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on E-mobility, Power Control and Smart Systems (ICEMPS)
abstract: Predicting Remaining Useful Life (RUL) for Lithium-cell NMC-LCO batteries in Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) is crucial for safe and efficient operation. Traditional methods rely on offline data analysis, limiting their accuracy in dynamic UAV flight conditions. This work proposes a Machine Learning (ML)-based approach for real-time RUL prediction, integrating online data acquisition. Remaining Useful Life (RUL) prediction is a numerical prediction, so the prediction of RUL fits into the regression technique. All regression models of ML are used in predicting the RUL. Sensor data from voltage, current, temperature, and vibration are fed into regression models of ML which include the KNN algorithm, SVM algorithm, Artificial Neural Networks (ANN), Decision Tree, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, and RNN networks with LSTM units, capturing temporal dependencies in battery degradation. The model is continuously updated using online data, improving its accuracy. The best fit for RUL prediction is analyzed to be a Random Forest. This approach addresses the challenges of dynamic UAV flight and diverse operating conditions, leading to more reliable and accurate RUL predictions for enhanced UAV safety and performance.

articleTitle: Malware Detection Using a Novel Machine Learning Dynamic Ensemble Classification Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on E-mobility, Power Control and Smart Systems (ICEMPS)
abstract: As the landscape of malware threats evolves., the need for effective detection methods becomes paramount. This study evaluates the performance of five ML algorithms Random Forest., SVM., DT., KNN., and Logistic Regression. A malware dataset from Kaggle was collected. The dataset., featuring a diverse array of features extracted from windows malware samples undergoes preprocessing and division into training and testing sets. Each algorithm is individually scrutinized for its malware detection capabilities., with metrics accuracy and recall. Later conventional ensemble learning techniques stacking classifier and voting classifier applied and achieved 98% and 97% accuracy. Subsequent to this initial analysis., a novel Dynamic Ensemble Classifier is introduced., dynamically selecting classifiers based on varying data characteristics. The proposed work compares the dynamic ensemble's performance against individual classifiers., demonstrating superior metrics. The accuracy achieved with proposed method is 99%. The dynamic ensemble exhibits adaptability to changing input data characteristics., offering a flexible and robust approach to malware detection. Experimental results showcased the efficacy of the dynamic ensemble., providing valuable insights for enhancing malware detection accuracy.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Based Capacity Prediction of Lithiumion Batteries Using Charging Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on E-mobility, Power Control and Smart Systems (ICEMPS)
abstract: This study explores the critical aspect of ensuring safety and reliability in lithium-ion batteries by accurately monitoring their State of Health (SOH). Because of the intricate nature of battery degradation, this research delves into data-driven methods as viable alternatives to traditional electrochemical modelling techniques. This study compares the efficacy of ARD Regressor, GPR, and ANN methods in predicting battery capacity, with a specific focus on charging time and temperature dynamics. Among the tested methods, Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) outperformed others, demonstrating better capability in capturing battery degradation trends, achieving a root mean square error (RMSE) of less or equal to 0.01 Ahr for three batteries.

articleTitle: Exploring the Influence of DJ-2D/3D Absorber Layer Thickness on TiO2-Based Perovskite Solar Cell Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on E-mobility, Power Control and Smart Systems (ICEMPS)
abstract: The exploration of a solar cell TiO2/(FA0.85MA0.15)Pb(I0.85Br0.15)/(FA0.85MA0.15)Pb(I0.85Br0.15) /Spiro-OMeTAD (DJ-2D/3D PSCs) through variations in the DJ-3D absorber layer thickness is the main focus of this work. One can use the Solar Cell Capacitance Simulator (SCAPS-1D) program to simulate the device. With DJ-2D and DJ-3D acting as the absorber or active layer, TiO2 acting as the electron transport layer (ETL), and Spiro-OMeTAD acting as the hole transport layer (HTL), the device's structure is optimized. Maximizing photon absorption from solar radiation is the objective. The performance of the device is being examined in relation to thickness changes. The maximum PCE is noted at the thickness value that is greatest. The DJ-2D/3D based cells' PV characteristics as a consequence are: FF: 81.61%, PCE: 22.09%, VOC: 1.076V, and JSC: 25.14mA/cm2.

articleTitle: Enhancing Network Security: A Comparative Analysis of Deep Learning and Machine Learning Models for Intrusion Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on E-mobility, Power Control and Smart Systems (ICEMPS)
abstract: The escalating reliance of computer networks on security systems exposes them to increasing threats. In response, an advanced security system is proposed, utilizing machine learning and deep learning techniques and leveraging the NSLKDD and CSE-CIC-IDS2018 datasets. Addressing the class imbalance challenges, the DSSTE algorithm is adopted to optimize model performance. Evaluation involves six, machine learning and deep learning methods: XGBoost, LSTM, Bi-LSTM, CNN, and VGG19, with a focus on assessing speed, false positive rate and detection efficiency. Experimental results underscore DSSTE's efficacy in mitigating class imbalance and enhancing overall intrusion detection. The proposed IDS, empowered by machine learning and DSSTE, ensures early detection and strengthens network security by countering intrusion attempts. Performance is compared with systems utilizing SMOTE and ADAASYN for data balancing.

articleTitle: Charging Up the Future: Capacitive and Inductive Wireless Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on E-mobility, Power Control and Smart Systems (ICEMPS)
abstract: Electric vehicles (EVs) have transformed the automotive landscape offering an eco-friendly and efficient alternative to traditional combustion engine vehicles so due to this it has got more acceptance in this current global scenario. This paper mainly focuses on capacitive and inductive techniques of wireless power transfer, its efficiency, power transfer techniques and topologies. Due to development in charging infrastructure the technological incentives continue to adopt EV for a cleaner and sustainable environment in future. WPT in EV is a groundbreaking technology that involves power transfer from source to batteries without the need of plugs and cables. Classification of charger stations into off-board and on-board which include IWPT and CWPT, enable us to understand the different technologies and infrastructure in charging EV. Each method has its advantages and limitations, contributing to the charging options available to the EV users.

articleTitle: Unlocking the Future of Stroke Diagnosis-Bayesian CNN and MRI Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on E-mobility, Power Control and Smart Systems (ICEMPS)
abstract: Stroke, as a life-threatening medical condition, necessitates rapid and accurate diagnosis to ensure timely treatment and optimal patient outcomes. In addressing the complex task of identifying strokes within Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) images, a Bayesian Convolutional Neural Network is introduced. This paper addressing the urgent demand for enhanced stroke detection in medical imaging. By harnessing the Bayesian framework, Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) achieves a notable accuracy rate of 92.98%, underscoring its effectiveness in delivering precise diagnoses. The approach distinguishes itself by its ability to measure prediction uncertainty, a critical element frequently disregarded in conventional models. This capability equips healthcare professionals with valuable information regarding the model's confidence in its stroke predictions, thereby enhancing clinical decision-making and ultimately elevating the standard of patient care in the context of stroke management.
